newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday May 28.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said that a meeting of political forces supporting prime minister Romano Prodi's coalition had not resolved differencies over Italy's three-year economic programme, particularly aspects affecting the welfare state. Bertinotti repeated his party's opposition to pension and social spending cuts (all).

* In talks on electoral reforms, centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance seem to have made an ouverture towards the idea of a strong prime minister, an idea backed by centre-left ruling coalition (all).
* Italian energy group ENI and electricity group Enel said they planned to float a stake in their new electricity production joint venture, but had not yet decided how much (all).

* In an interview, Alessandro Profumo, managing director of banking group Credito Italiano, said the bank was not planning, at least in the short-term, to buy stakes in other banking groups. He also said the bank was not interested in the acquisition of Credito Bergamasco from Credit Lyonnais (Corriere della Sera).
* San Paolo di Brescia is reportedly interested in the acquisition of a major stake in Credito Bergamasco, the bank sold by French group Credit Lyonnais (Corriere della Sera).
* Mobile phone operator Omnitel said it posted a 589 trillion lire loss in 1996, in line with the group's expectations (Sole 24 Ore).
* German insurer Allianz AG Holding said Roberto Gavazzi had decided to step down from its management board on June 30 and would leave the country for a position in Italy (all).
* Insurer group Ina said it posted a 505 billion lire consolidated net profit in 1996, 22.6 percent higher than in 1995 (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
